idea: Signs of a hidden water leak
title: Diagnostic Tip: The Water Meter Leak Test
description: A sudden jump in your water bill or damp spots on walls often point to a hidden supply line leak. Before tearing open drywall or excavating slabs, perform a water meter leak test. Turn off every tap, appliance, and fixture inside and outside the property. Locate your main water meter and examine the small flow indicator—often a small triangular or star-shaped wheel on the dial face. If this low-flow indicator rotates while no water is actively being drawn, water is escaping under pressure downstream. This simple test confirms a hidden supply leak before any invasive repair work begins.
image_prompt: Professional technical close-up photography of a residential water meter assembly, vertical 9:16 aspect ratio. The main focal point is the clear glass face of a brass analog water meter displaying clean numerical registers and a distinct red triangular low-flow leak indicator wheel near the center of the dial. The meter is properly installed along a copper and brass pipe assembly with realistic threaded brass couplings and a lever-handle ball valve on the inlet side. Sharp focus on the meter dial, natural daylight with clear clarity, professional plumbing working environment. Generous clean visual space at top and bottom for text placement. Photorealistic, physically accurate pipe geometry, no text, no visual labels, no watermarks, no logos, no fake branding.
visual_story: The visual focuses on a realistic water meter face and pipe connection assembly. The viewer is trained to spot the small low-flow indicator wheel located on the dial. By showing a clear, centered, and physically correct water meter setup, the visual teaches viewers exactly where visual evidence of hidden water movement appears on a standard meter.

on_image_text.hook: How to Confirm a Hidden Supply Leak
on_image_text.explanation: If the small low-flow indicator wheel turns while every fixture is shut off, pressurized water is escaping downstream.
on_image_text.takeaway: Check your meter first to confirm a leak before opening walls or breaking concrete.
